name: Ugur Sahin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Uğur Şahin is CEO and cofounder of German biotech firm BioNTech, which partnered with Pfizer to produce the first Covid-19 vaccine approved in the US.
Şahin led BioNTech to start on a vaccine for the coronavirus in early 2020; it partnered with Pfizer in March 2020 and got approval in December.
Şahin, who was born in Turkey and grew up in Germany, owns about 17% of BioNTech, which went public on the Nasdaq in October 2019.
In 2001 Şahin and his immunologist wife, ?zlem T'reci, cofounded Ganymed Pharmaceuticals; Astellas Pharma acquired Ganymed in 2016 for $460 million.
Şahin and his wife T'reci cofounded BioNTech in 2008, backed by German billionaire brothers Thomas and Andreas Struengmann.
forbes_facts: Sahin's parents worked in a Ford factory in Germany; he was trained as a doctor and worked as a researcher and a professor.
Germany's billionaire Struengmann brothers have backed both of Sahin's drug companies: Ganymed Pharmaceuticals and BioNTech SE.

name: Christian Haub
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Christian Haub runs his family's Tengelmann Group, a retail conglomerate that began with a shop opened in Muelheim an der Ruhr in 1867 and today employs more than 70,000.
Its operations include home-improvement chain OBI; clothing and non-food discounter KiK; online retailer babymarkt.de; and food production company No Meat Factory.
The group also invests in startups and is active in services (energy, plus audits and consulting), property management and real estate development.
Older brother Karl-Erivan and Christian had taken over as co-CEOs in 2000. In 2018, Karl-Erivan went missing while on a ski tour. In 2021, he was declared dead.
In 2021 Christian bought an additional stake in Tengelmann 21 from Karl-Erivan's two children, reportedly paying as much as $1.6 billion. He is now its largest shareholder with a 68.67% stake.
forbes_facts: Erivan Haub had strong ties to Tacoma, WA, where his sons were born. He was a major contributor to UW-Tacoma, the Museum of Glass and the LeMay Automobile Museum.

name: Jai Hari
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2018)
forbes_bio: Siblings Jai Hari and Yadu Hari Dalmia control the Dalmia Bharat Group, inherited from their father Jaidayal Dalmia, who set it up in 1939.
Their listed Dalmia Bharat is the fourth-largest cement producer in the country, with 12 factories.
The brothers also have an interest in sugar through Dalmia Bharat Sugar.
Yadu Hari Dalmia's son Puneet manages the cement business. Jai Hari Dalmia's son Gautam manages the sugar unit.
forbes_facts: The cement company sells limited edition art pieces made from cement.
Dalmia Bharat has committed to using 100% renewable power by 2030.

name: John Tyson
sec_insider_companies: TYSON FOODS, INC. (TSN) - Chairman of the Board
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: John Tyson is chairman of Tyson Foods, the processor that breeds, slaughters and sells meat that ends up in grocery stores across America
The conglomerate owns beloved brands like Hillshire Farms, Jimmy Dean and Aidells sausages.
Tyson is known for its chicken, but the company also produces approximately 20% of the beef and pork in the U.S.
In 2019, Tyson Foods debuted its own alternative meat line Raised & Rooted, including plant-based nuggets.
Tyson Foods was originally founded by John's grandfather in 1935. John served as CEO of the company from 2000 to 2006.
forbes_facts: Following in the footsteps of his late father, John Tyson is an avid art collector whose collection includes the likes of Warhol, Lichtenstein and de Kooning.
Tyson began working at Tyson Foods at 13, transferring eggs to incubators in the hatchery and vaccinating chickens on the farm.

name: Jaroslav Hascak
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Jaroslav Hascak is cofounder of Penta Investments, which has investments in the healthcare, banking, real estate and aeronautical industries.
Penta, which he controls with Mark Dospiva, has controlling stakes in Privatbanka, pharmacy chain Dr. Max and sports betting operator Fortuna.
Hascak and Dospiva (a Czech national) were both studying in Beijing and got started by importing Chinese textiles to chain stores in then-Czechoslovakia.
During Slovakia's 1996 privatization process, Penta gained control over the nation's biggest fund, paying only 20 percent of its market value.
A hands-on manager, he has created a very competitive culture within the company, called System Up or Out, designed to get rid of weak performers.
forbes_facts: Hascak spent one-tenth of his early earnings to buy his first car, a Fiat Uno; the rest he invested into the stock brokerage business.
Hascak typically works 12 hours a day, six days a week.

name: Katharina Andresen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2026); Wikidata (2017)
forbes_bio: Katharina Andresen, born 1995, is one of the world's youngest billionaires.
She and her sister Alexandra, one year her junior,  each inherited 42% of the family-owned investment company Ferd.
The sisters' father Johan still runs the company and controls 70% of the votes via a dual-class share structure.
Ferd runs hedge funds, is an active investor on the Nordic stock exchange, and has private equity investments.
forbes_facts: In 2017 Katharina was stopped by police at tony ski resort Hafjell and was found to be driving under the influence and was eventually fined $32,000.
The Andresen family has been a household name in Norway for over 100 years, primarily known for its tobacco brand, which they sold in 2005.

name: Hao Hong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Hao Hong is the chairman of Shenzhen-listed Asymchem Laboratories, which provides pharmaceutical outsourcing services.
Hao Hong's wife Ye Song is a non-executive board member and serves as a board member of several Asymchem subsidiaries.
Asymchem went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2016; it added a listing at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2021.
Hao Hong holds a Ph.D. in pharmaceutical chemistry from the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences.
Hao Hong founded the company in the United States in 1995.
forbes_facts: Hao Hong's wife Ye Song received a PhD from North Carolina State University in 1999.

name: Lucy Stitzer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Lucy Stitzer chairs Waycrosse, the investment company of the Cargill and MacMillan families, one of the 10 richest clans in America.
Stitzer owns an estimated 3% stake in Cargill, the largest food company in the world.
She's one of four billionaire sisters who inherited stakes in the company from their father W. Duncan MacMillan, who died in 2006.
Her great-great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, founded the business as a single grain warehouse on the end of an Iowa railroad line in 1865.
The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.

forbes_bio: Gan is cofounder and chairman of Shanghai-listed Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals.
Founded in 1998, the company produces insulin and injection pens and is publicly traded.
Gan graduated from Peking University and later became a teacher in the biology department.
Gan holds a PhD from Michigan State University and worked for Merck before starting Gan & Lee.

name: Nikil Viswanathan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Nikil Viswanathan cofounded Alchemy, whose software powers thousands of blockchain-based Web3 companies.
Alchemy, founded in 2020, was valued by private investors at $10.2 billion in February 2022; Viswanathan owns an estimated 26% stake.
Forbes estimates that Alchemy is now worth around $6 billion as the valuations of private tech companies have generally fallen from their peaks in early 2022.
In December 2021, the company announced the launch of Alchemy Ventures, which invests in current clients with the goal of bootstrapping the industry.
Viswanathan and cofounder Joe Lau, both Stanford grads, found initial success with meetup app Down to Lunch, briefly topping the Apple Store charts.
forbes_facts: Alchemy's team consists of engineers from Google, Facebook, Microsoft, LinkedIn and Pinterest, some of them college friends of Viswanathan and Lau.
